clusters.title: Forgeable Public/Private Tokens
clusters.rationale: The jws library at version 0.2.6 is vulnerable to token forgery via CVE-2016-1000223 and CVE-2025-65945. This poses a severe risk of authentication bypass across the application.
fix: Upgrade jws to version 3.2.3 in package-lock.json.
Rebuild application dependencies and update Node.js.
Test token generation and signature verification flows against existing tokens.

clusters.title: Found data from an Express or Next web request flowing to `eval`. If this data is user-controllable this can lead to execution of arbitrary system commands in the context of your application process.
clusters.rationale: Untrusted web request data flows directly into eval() in routes/userProfile.ts, creating a critical remote code execution vulnerability. An attacker can execute arbitrary code inside the application container.
fix: Remove the eval() call from routes/userProfile.ts immediately.
Refactor the code to use safe parsing logic such as JSON.parse() or static lookups.
Sanitize and strictly validate all user input prior to processing.
Add automated tests to prevent dynamic code execution patterns.

clusters.title: nodejs-jsonwebtoken: verification step bypass with an altered token
clusters.rationale: Severely outdated jsonwebtoken versions in package-lock.json permit token verification bypasses including CVE-2015-9235 and CVE-2022-23539. This presents a critical authentication vulnerability for an e-commerce API.
fix: Upgrade jsonwebtoken in package-lock.json to 9.0.0.
Verify token verification calls in Node.js explicitly enforce expected algorithms.
Run integration tests covering authorization and token parsing.

clusters.title: Raw SQL built with template-literal interpolation is passed to sequelize.query(). Pass user input through `replacements` or `bind` parameters instead.
clusters.rationale: Raw SQL queries in routes/login.ts concatenate user input directly, leading to SQL injection. An attacker could exploit this to manipulate database transactions or access sensitive data.
fix: Inspect sequelize.query() statements in routes/login.ts.
Replace template literal interpolation with Sequelize bind or replacement parameters.
Validate and sanitize all incoming request parameters used in queries.

clusters.title: Raw SQL built with template-literal interpolation is passed to sequelize.query(). Pass user input through `replacements` or `bind` parameters instead.
clusters.rationale: Template-literal interpolation inside sequelize.query() in routes/search.ts exposes the application to SQL injection. This allows untrusted input to execute arbitrary SQL commands against the database.
fix: Inspect raw query logic in routes/search.ts.
Switch from string interpolation to parameterized queries using replacements or bind options.
Verify query outputs with automated regression tests.

clusters.title: Untrusted user input in MongoDB $where operator can result in NoSQL JavaScript Injection.
clusters.rationale: Untrusted input in a MongoDB $where clause enables server-side JavaScript execution and potential database compromise. Without source code, the exact exploitability cannot be confirmed.
fix: Remove dynamic string concatenation within the $where clause in routes/trackOrder.ts.
Rewrite query logic to use standard MongoDB query operators like $eq instead of JavaScript expressions.
Enforce strict schema validation and typing on all incoming user parameters.

clusters.title: A hardcoded password in plain text is identified. Store it properly in an environment variable.
clusters.rationale: A hardcoded plaintext password was detected in frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts. Storing secrets directly in application code risks exposure through source control and image inspection.
fix: Remove the hardcoded secret from frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts.
Inject the credential via environment variables or Kubernetes secrets.
Rotate the exposed password immediately across all environments.

clusters.title: Untrusted user input in findOne() function can result in NoSQL Injection.
clusters.rationale: Passing unvalidated input directly to findOne() can allow NoSQL operator injection and unauthorized record retrieval. Without source code, it is uncertain whether input validation is performed upstream.
fix: Validate that query parameters in routes/address.ts are primitive types rather than objects.
Sanitize incoming user input with mongo-sanitize or an equivalent library.
Apply strict request schema validation using Zod or Joi.

clusters.title: Untrusted user input in findOne() function can result in NoSQL Injection.
clusters.rationale: Passing unvalidated user inputs to findOne() in routes/basket.ts may allow attackers to inject MongoDB operators to bypass query restrictions. Without inspecting source code, exploitability remains unconfirmed.
fix: Cast or strictly type search parameters to primitive values in routes/basket.ts.
Strip query operators from user-supplied data using mongo-sanitize.
Implement schema validation on incoming request bodies and query strings.

clusters.title: Untrusted user input in findOne() function can result in NoSQL Injection.
clusters.rationale: Allowing unvalidated input into findOne() in routes/basketItems.ts introduces risk of NoSQL injection and data exposure. Without source code access, we cannot verify if parameter sanitization exists.
fix: Ensure query arguments in routes/basketItems.ts do not accept nested object operators.
Apply mongo-sanitize to strip disallowed query keys from user input.

clusters.title: nodejs-lodash: prototype pollution in defaultsDeep function leading to modifying properties
clusters.rationale: Lodash 2.4.2 in package-lock.json is vulnerable to prototype pollution and command injection including CVE-2019-10744 and CVE-2021-23337. These flaws can lead to denial of service or unexpected runtime behavior.
fix: Update lodash dependency in package-lock.json to 4.18.0.
Check Node.js for deprecated lodash v2 function signatures.
Run unit tests to ensure application stability after upgrade.

clusters.title: nodejs-moment: Regular expression denial of service
clusters.rationale: Moment 2.0.0 is affected by CVE-2016-4055, CVE-2017-18214, and CVE-2022-24785, leading to potential denial of service or path traversal. Without reviewing application code, it is uncertain if untrusted input reaches date or locale parsing.
fix: Upgrade moment to version 2.29.2 in package-lock.json.
Update lockfiles and rebuild the bundled assets in Node.js.
Run unit and regression test suites covering date and locale operations.

clusters.title: tar: node-tar: Denial of Service via crafted gzip bomb
clusters.rationale: The tar package is vulnerable to denial-of-service and file-extraction issues including CVE-2026-23745 and CVE-2026-73566. Impact depends on whether the application extracts untrusted archives in Node.js.
fix: Review archive handling logic in Node.js.
Update tar dependency in package-lock.json to 7.5.21.
Rebuild container image and test archive unpacking.

clusters.title: crypto-js: PBKDF2 1,000 times weaker than specified in 1993 and 1.3M times weaker than current standard
clusters.rationale: The crypto-js package at version 3.3.0 utilizes weak PBKDF2 defaults under CVE-2023-46233 and CVE-2026-71851. This makes stored password hashes significantly more susceptible to offline cracking.
fix: Update crypto-js in package-lock.json to 4.2.0.
Review PBKDF2 iteration configurations in Node.js to ensure high iteration counts.
Execute cryptographic test suites to verify signature and hash validity.

clusters.title: Ensure VPC subnets do not assign public IP by default
clusters.rationale: Terraform definitions in infrastructure/terraform/networking.tf and terraform/networking.tf enable public IP assignment by default on VPC subnets. This increases exposure of container hosts or internal cluster resources to the Internet.
fix: Inspect subnet resource blocks in infrastructure/terraform/networking.tf and terraform/networking.tf.
Set map_public_ip_on_launch to false for non-public subnets.
Apply Terraform changes and verify subnet routing configurations.

clusters.title: Ensure ECS containers are limited to read-only access to root filesystems
clusters.rationale: Allowing containers writable root filesystems increases lateral movement potential following container compromise. This is an infrastructure defense-in-depth misconfiguration.
fix: Locate container definitions within infrastructure/terraform/main.tf and terraform/main.tf.
Set readonlyRootFilesystem to true for all ECS container definitions.
Mount temporary writable directories using tmpfs or dedicated volumes where needed.

clusters.title: Ensure CloudWatch log groups retains logs for at least 1 year
clusters.rationale: Short CloudWatch log retention limits incident response and compliance audit capabilities but poses no direct exploitability. This represents an infrastructure hardening deficit.
fix: Open infrastructure/terraform/main.tf and terraform/main.tf in the repository.
Update or add retention_in_days to at least 365 on all aws_cloudwatch_log_group resources.
Apply and verify the updated Terraform plan.

clusters.title: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
clusters.rationale: The application does not serve a Content Security Policy header. While not directly exploitable by itself, it removes defense-in-depth protection against cross-site scripting.
fix: Add a Content-Security-Policy header in the web application response middleware.
Configure directives such as default-src and script-src to match application assets.
Test the policy in report-only mode before enforcing in production.

clusters.title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy Header Missing or Invalid
clusters.rationale: Missing the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header can allow cross-origin browsing contexts to interact with the window object. This is a low-impact defense-in-depth finding.
fix: Configure the web server or reverse proxy to return the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header.
Set the header value to same-origin or same-origin-allow-popups.
Verify header delivery across endpoints with browser developer tools.

clusters.title: Dangerous JS Functions
clusters.rationale: The scanner flagged potentially risky client-side JavaScript functions, which only become dangerous if combined with DOM-based injection sinks. Without evidence of untrusted input flows, this is a low-priority hygiene alert.
fix: Audit frontend scripts for direct invocations of eval or innerHTML.
Replace dynamic code evaluation with safe DOM manipulation methods like textContent.
Deploy a Content Security Policy that restricts unsafe-eval and unsafe-inline.
